newsitem.title: FRANCE: BNP sets up pension fund ahead of new law.
newsitem.headline: BNP sets up pension fund ahead of new law.

text.p: BNP bank said on Tuesday it was setting up a pension fund "Natio-Retraite" in preparation for legislation to allow private funds to provide retirement pensions in France for the first time.

BNP managing director Baudoin Prot told a news conference the market for such funds could be 20-25 billion francs a year within three or four years and that BNP would be happy if it could take five percent of the market.
Draft legislation, which is most of the way through parliament, will permit the creation of private, pre-funded pension funds.

Parliamentary sources say the National Assembly and Senate will state their final position on the bill on February 25, following the bill's passage through a mixed committee from the two houses of parliament, which begins on February 5.

State-owned insurer Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance (CNP) said separately that it expected the market to fall short of some forecasts with about 15-20 billion francs going into such funds in the first year.

It said the reform of France's pensions system "is a little more modest than we were hoping. At the outset we were hoping for more significant business but the take-off will be slower than expected," chief executive Pierre Darnis said.
CNP had initially forecast a "cruising speed" of 30-50 billion francs a year but Darnis told reporters on Tuesday that this figure would have to be revised downwards.

The French Bank Association (AFB) said in a recent report that it expected 60 percent of small- and medium-sized firms and three-quarters of big firms to subscribe and that 55 percent of non-managerial employees could get involved and 66 percent of those at managerial level.
